newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Daiwa sees Votorantim group as likely CVRD winner.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa sees Votorantim group as likely CVRD winner.

text.p: A consortium led by Brazil's Votorantim group was likely to win the bidding on a controlling stake in state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce, Daiwa Securities America Inc said in a report.

Daiwa analyst Eveline Freire Gerck said the consortium is favored in the privatization auction over a group led by local steel firm CSN due to its "greater capital resources and strong political support."
The sale of a 45-percent voting stake in CVRD was slated for Tuesday at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange but may be delayed by a host of legal challenges.

The Votorantim-led group also includes Anglo-American Corp of South Africa, Caemi, Banco Safra, Bozano Simonsen, Brazilian pension funds Sistel and Centrus, and a group of Japanese steel firms led by Nippon Steel.

Freire Gerck said the privatization model chosen by Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) was adopted to protect CVRD's competitive advantages as well as quiet opposition to the selloff. Moreover, "the two-step auction process envisioned appreciation of CVRD's equity," she wrote.
But the model also hurt the selloff and the price of CVRD shares by scaring away other potential bidders, she added.
"The many restrictions imposed by the government ..., in our opinion, have been adverse to the strategy for share-price appreciation," Freire Gerck wrote.
"Major foreign companies lost interest in bidding for CVRD's shares due to the goivernment's requirements for acquiring and managing CVRD," she added.

Freire Gerck said Brazil almost was left with just one consortium of companies, led by Votorantim, to bid for control of CVRD at the minimum price of 26.67 reais per share. "However, the government intervened, forcing Brazilian pension funds which had been prepared to back Votorantim to split into two groups," she said.
The group led by CSN, known as Companhia Siderurgica Nacional, also includes NationsBank, Suzano, pension funds Previ, Petros, Funcesp and Funcef, Opportunity Asset Management and Gencor.

According to Freire Gerck, bidding is unlikely to push CVRD's common share higher than 10-30 percent over the base price. "The government already has signalled an expectation of a 10-15 percent premium over the minimum price as a reasonable profit," she said.
